steps.text: The centered approach works better than approaching the peg’s grasp site: lowering the gripper over the peg’s midpoint and closing lets the peg rise with the hand. I’m using the peg’s observed pose to carry its head to the socket target, with elevated waypoints to clear the box.

from mw_runtime import Session
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
s=Session()
def status(label):
 o=s.observe();b=o['bodies']['peg'];head=s.env._get_site_pos('pegHead').copy();tcp=o['tcp'];
 print(label,'n',len(s.actions),'tcp',tcp,'pegbody',b['position'],'quat',b['quaternion_wxyz'],'head',head,'goal',o['goal'],'reward',s.result()['info'])
 Image.fromarray(s.render()).save('/app/output/'+label+'.png')
 return o,b,head
s.move([.0376,.511,.10],-1,40)
s.move([.0376,.511,0.0],-1,50)
for _ in range(20):s.step([0,0,0,1])
status('attempt_closed')
s.move([.0376,.511,.15],1,50)
o,b,head=status('attempt_lifted')
# Calculate rotation of local head offset using scipy Rotation (wxyz -> xyzw)
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
q=b['quaternion_wxyz'];R=Rotation.from_quat([q[1],q[2],q[3],q[0]])
offset=R.apply([-.1,0,0])
target_body=o['goal']-offset
body=b['position'].copy();tcp=o['tcp'].copy(); hand_offset=tcp-body
print('planned body',target_body,'tcp offset',hand_offset)
# raise peg vertically while carrying, then translate over hole at safe height
for i,desired_body in enumerate([
 np.array([body[0],body[1],.24]),
 np.array([target_body[0],target_body[1],.24]),
 target_body,
]):
 des_tcp=desired_body+hand_offset
 o=s.move(des_tcp,1,50,tolerance=.003)
 status('attempt_waypoint'+str(i))
 if s.result()['success']:break
print('RESULT',s.result())
s.save('/app/output/trial_insert.npz')

 # update hand-to-body offset only to account for any tiny grasp motion
 handoff=o['tcp']-b['position']
 if s.result()['success']:break
print('RESULT',s.result())

note: Codex ran without our model gateway: this log is rebuilt from Harbor's trajectory of its session, so request times are approximate (each request is drawn up to when its answer was recorded) and failed requests are not listed. The replay is our trusted render of the submitted trajectory in a fresh container (corner and corner3 cameras, rotated 180°; 80 fps = real time).
